issues.description: Attribute mismatch for RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings: The UML in the problem statement declares the attribute "numberOfLoopings" as type int (problem_statement.md line 27), but the reference implementation (solution) declares the private field as type long (RollerCoaster.java line 5) and the getter getNumberOfLoopings() returns long (RollerCoaster.java line 12). The solution's constructor still accepts an int parameter (RollerCoaster.java line 7), which highlights an inconsistency between the UML specification and the reference code. This mismatch can confuse students about which type to implement (int vs long) and may cause tests or expected signatures based on the UML to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfLoopings consistent between the UML and the reference implementation. Preferred fix: change the field and getter in src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java from long to int (update the declaration to `private int numberOfLoopings;` and change `public long getNumberOfLoopings()` to `public int getNumberOfLoopings()`). Ensure any assignments and usages remain type-compatible. Alternatively, if long is intended, update the UML/problem statement to declare numberOfLoopings: long and document the reason for using long.
